analysis.title: The Vault: A correction, not a capitulation
key_insights: ANZ sees the Fed rate-hiking cycle and a stronger USD as short-term drags on gold. It expects the weakness to be temporary and keeps its positive medium to long-term view, citing gold's role as a risk diversifier amid fiscal and debt concerns.
Gold's rally after the US midterm elections has faded as focus shifts to Fed tightening. Higher inflation prints strengthened the case for more hikes and pushed gold lower.

ANZ's base case is a 25bp Fed hike in December and 25bp hikes in January and March. It cannot rule out 50bp in December. The market prices about 80bp of tightening this cycle, and a 50bp move would deepen the near-term gold correction.
A recovery in equities after the tech-linked sell-off would add pressure on gold flows.
ANZ expects renewed strategic and retail buying to provide a gold floor around USD3,600/oz, with prices moving toward USD4,800/oz in 2027.
WGC Q3 total gold demand was 1,369t, the highest this year and marginally below a year earlier, with prices averaging about USD4,150/oz.
Q3 total investment demand was 479t, above the five-year quarterly average of 395t but below 2025's levels. Bar & coin eased while ETF flows rebounded, with holdings up 211t in Q3.

ANZ expects European ETF flows to stay positive and North American (mainly US) holdings to decline in Q4. China's flows should stay resilient, and India's ETF flows should soften after mutual funds suspended new Gold Fund of Funds subscriptions in mid-October.
Bar & coin demand fell 60t y/y to 267t in Q3, with India down 40% to 55t and China up 7% to 79t. ANZ expects Q4 below 300t, nearly 130t lower than a year ago.
CME speculative liquidation has added nearly 200t to the market, but net longs remain elevated at 533t. ANZ expects speculators to cut a further 200t, which could worsen the price fall.
ANZ raised its 2026 central bank purchase forecast to 950t from 850t after Q3 buying of 321t. It expects Q4 buying above 300t.

PBoC bought 26t in October, the highest since 2023. China's holdings are 2,435t, nearly 10% of reserves, and ANZ expects faster buying as prices fall. Poland reached its 700t target in October and says accumulation will continue.
Jewellery demand fell to 313t in Q3, the weakest third quarter. Year-to-date demand is down 19% to 889t, and full-year demand is likely below 1,400t.
Silver is a high-beta play on gold. Soft industrial demand and sufficient inventories mean a sustained rebound depends on a gold recovery.
Solar silver demand is expected to fall nearly 19% to 151moz in 2026, with silver intensity down 17%. Solar's share of silver demand is projected at 14% from 17%.

Silver inventories are ample. The COMEX inventory to open interest ratio is 50% against a 20-25% historical average, London free-floating stocks rose with 47.7moz of ETF liquidation, and Shanghai stocks added nearly 35moz.

The precious metals scorecard is bearish on gold fundamentals, USD, US outlook, investment demand and technicals, and bullish on geopolitical risk, China demand and central bank purchases. Silver is bearish on most indicators, platinum is mixed to bullish on supply, and palladium is bearish.

sector_views.rationale: Near-term bearish on Fed hikes, a stronger USD and investment liquidation. Medium to long-term positive on central bank buying and fiscal concerns.
Soft industrial demand, ample inventories and a downward technical trend. A rebound depends on gold.
Constrained South African mine supply should help prices stabilise, but ETF holdings are declining and sentiment is bearish.
Demand headwinds from EV adoption and accelerated futures liquidation with shorts building.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Supports a hawkish Fed tilt, negative for gold.
Strongest pace since mid-2021, supporting the case for further hikes.
Up from below 2% in August, broadening inflation strengthens the case for Fed hikes.

macro_indicators.reading: 25bp in December, 25bp in January, 25bp in March
macro_indicators.interpretation: A 50bp December hike cannot be ruled out and would deepen the gold correction.

risk_factors: A 50bp Fed hike in December would deepen the gold correction.
A recovery in equities after the tech sell-off would pressure gold flows.
Further liquidation of CME speculative positions, about 200t more.
Gold-backed ETF liquidation, especially in North America.
India's mutual fund suspension of Gold Fund of Funds subscriptions could slow inflows.
Weak AI-linked and solar silver demand, with community opposition and power constraints threatening AI infrastructure build-out.
Upside energy price risk from the US-Iran truce uncertainty keeps inflation elevated.
vol_and_positioning: CME gold net-long positions are 533t after nearly 200t of liquidation, versus a low of 200t in 2023 and 2022. ANZ expects speculators to cut a further 200t.
Silver tactical positions have declined, adding more than 50moz to the market.
Palladium futures show accelerated liquidation and building shorts.
Gold ETF holdings are elevated and at risk of liquidation, especially in North America.
geopolitical: Uncertainty over a lasting US-Iran truce keeps energy-price risks skewed to the upside and inflation concerns alive.
Political gridlock is raising uncertainty around government funding, debt negotiations and the fiscal outlook.
Republican control of Congress until early January leaves the policy backdrop largely unchanged.
Geopolitical fragmentation is driving structural central bank gold buying.
Poland reached its 700t gold target in October and says accumulation will continue.
China is decreasing its US Treasury holdings and increasing gold reserves.

tension_points.bull_case: Strategic and retail buying should provide a floor around USD3,600/oz and lift prices toward USD4,800/oz in 2027. Central bank buying is structural and fiscal and debt concerns support gold as a risk diversifier.
tension_points.bear_case: Fed hikes, a stronger USD, ETF liquidation and a further 200t of CME speculative selling could deepen the near-term correction, and a 50bp December hike would add to it.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A 50bp Fed hike in December, or a further 200t of speculative liquidation, would deepen the correction and test the USD3,600/oz floor.

theme_stances.key_argument: Fed rate hikes and a stronger USD weigh on non-yielding gold in the short term, though the weakness is seen as temporary.
theme_stances.evidence: We see this weakness as temporary

theme_stances.key_argument: Reserve buying is driven by structural factors like geopolitical fragmentation and debt sustainability, so it stays solid at lower prices.
theme_stances.evidence: Central bank stockpiling to remain solid at lower prices
